raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
The ModelOpt NVFP4 checkpoint of Muse Spark Open keeps the routed experts of layers 0 and 61 in BF16 (24 GiB each). With the opt-in `muse_spark_quantize_bf16_experts` text-config field (set through --hf-overrides), those layers are built as NVFP4 and their experts are quantized while they load, so all 62 MoE layers run the NVFP4 TRT-LLM MoE and the weights shrink by ~34 GiB. Attention, projections and norms of those layers stay BF16.

Each full expert is quantized on the GPU, one at a time, into the ModelOpt checkpoint layout with the existing online NVFP4 quantizer (one global scale per expert, shared by gate and up), then goes through the normal NVFP4 weight loader. The quantized tensors stay on the GPU until the loader copies them into the parameters: copying them back to fresh pageable host memory stalled late in loading on GB300 (Grace). Quantizing before the TP/EP split matches an offline requantized checkpoint at any TP size. The checkpoint has no activation calibration for these layers and the TRT-LLM NVFP4 MoE takes static input scales, so after loading they take the max input scales of the two nearest calibrated NVFP4 layers.

The field is rejected with MegaMoE and off SM100, and is documented in the ModelOpt quantization page.


Assisted-by: Claude

## Claude Code Review

This pull request is from a fork — automated review is disabled. A repository maintainer can comment `@claude review` to run a one-time review.

Could we use existing online quantization infrastructure here?

Namely:
- `--quantization-config.targets`:
```
     --quantization-config '{"targets":{"*layers.0.feed_forward.experts*":"nvfp4_per_token", "*layers.61.feed_forward.experts*":"nvfp4_per_token"}}'
```
- (re-)quantization of checkpoints https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/60276 https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/64378

In https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/32412 / https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/32029 and followup https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/52167, the goal is to have vLLM frontend not be dependent on the model producer library (modelopt, compressed-tensors, etc.), and if possible not on the model arch.

As muse spark MOE is a normal `RoutedExperts`, the API at https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/main/vllm/model_executor/layers/quantization/online is the one that fits naturally.

A welcome extension would be to have `Nvfpv4OnlineMoEMethod` & NVFP4 oracle compatible with Muse, if any change is needed (or have `MuseSparkNvfp4OnlineMoEMethod(Nvfpv4OnlineMoEMethod)`, alternatively, but using oracle would be cleaner)

+## Muse Spark BF16 routed experts
+
+The ModelOpt NVFP4 checkpoint of Muse Spark Open
+(`meta-models/Muse-Spark-Open-816B-A42B-NVFP4`) keeps the routed experts of
+layers 0 and 61 in BF16 (24 GiB each). To run them as NVFP4 too, set the
+`muse_spark_quantize_bf16_experts` text-config field (off by default):
+
+```bash
+vllm serve meta-models/Muse-Spark-Open-816B-A42B-NVFP4 \
+    --hf-overrides '{"text_config": {"muse_spark_quantize_bf16_experts": true}}'
+```
+
+vLLM then quantizes those experts to NVFP4 while loading, one expert at a time
+on the GPU, so all MoE layers run the FlashInfer TRT-LLM NVFP4 MoE and the
+weights shrink by about 34 GiB. The checkpoint has no activation calibration
+for these layers, so each takes the largest static input scales of its two
+nearest NVFP4 layers. The other modules of those layers stay BF16. This needs
+an SM100-family GPU and is not supported with the `deep_gemm_mega_moe` MoE
+backend.
+

+    # Each max sits on a single expert.
+    w13 = torch.full((4, 2), scale / 2)

+    w2[2] = scale / 2

+def quantize_experts_to_nvfp4(
+    weight: torch.Tensor, device: torch.device | str
+) -> tuple[torch.Tensor, torch.Tensor, torch.Tensor]:
+    """Quantize experts ``[E, R, C]`` to the ModelOpt NVFP4 checkpoint layout.
+
+    Experts move to ``device`` one at a time. Returns, on ``device``, packed
+    E2M1 ``[E, R, C // 2]``, block scales ``[E, R, C // 16]`` and one global
+    scale per expert ``[E]``.
+    """
+    # Copying each expert back to fresh pageable host memory can stall late in
+    # loading on Grace (GB300); the weight loader copies from ``device``.
+    num_experts, rows, cols = weight.shape
+    packed = torch.empty(
+        (num_experts, rows, cols // 2), dtype=torch.uint8, device=device
+    )
+    block_scale = torch.empty(
+        (num_experts, rows, cols // 16), dtype=torch.float8_e4m3fn, device=device
+    )
+    global_scale = torch.empty(num_experts, dtype=torch.float32, device=device)
+    for expert in range(num_experts):
+        quantized = _quantize_moe_weight_to_nvfp4(
+            weight[expert : expert + 1].to(device)
+        )
+        for out, value in zip(
+            (packed, block_scale, global_scale), quantized, strict=True
+        ):
+            out[expert].copy_(value[0])
+    return packed, block_scale, global_scale
+
+
+class MuseSparkBf16AsNvFp4RoutedExperts(MuseSparkRoutedExperts):
+    """NVFP4 experts for a BF16 layer of an NVFP4 checkpoint, quantized on load.
+
+    Whole experts are quantized before the TP/EP split, as an offline
+    requantized checkpoint would be. The checkpoint has no input scales for
+    them; see ``set_uncalibrated_input_scales``.
+    """
+
+    def _get_quant_method(
+        self,
+        prefix: str,
+        quant_config: QuantizationConfig | None,
+        moe_config: FusedMoEConfig,
+    ) -> FusedMoEMethodBase:
+        assert isinstance(quant_config, ModelOptNvFp4Config)
+        return MuseSparkModelOptNvFp4FusedMoE(quant_config, moe_config)
+
+    def load_weights(
+        self, weights: Iterable[tuple[str, torch.Tensor]]
+    ) -> Iterable[str]:
+        return super().load_weights(self._quantize_bf16_weights(weights))
+
+    def _quantize_bf16_weights(
+        self, weights: Iterable[tuple[str, torch.Tensor]]
+    ) -> Iterable[tuple[str, torch.Tensor]]:
+        for name, tensor in weights:
+            if name not in ("w13_weight", "w2_weight"):
+                yield name, tensor
+                continue
+            packed, block_scale, global_scale = quantize_experts_to_nvfp4(
+                tensor, self.moe_config.device
+            )
+            stem = name.removesuffix("_weight")
+            yield name, packed
+            yield f"{stem}_weight_scale", block_scale
+            # Gate and up share their expert's global scale.
+            yield (
+                f"{stem}_weight_scale_2",
+                global_scale if stem == "w2" else global_scale[:, None].expand(-1, 2),
+            )
+
+
+def set_uncalibrated_input_scales(
+    input_scales: Mapping[int, tuple[torch.Tensor, torch.Tensor]],
+    uncalibrated: Collection[int],
+) -> None:
+    """Set static input scales for NVFP4 MoE layers with no activation calibration.
+
+    ``input_scales`` maps every NVFP4 MoE layer to its ``(w13, w2)`` input
+    scales. The TRT-LLM NVFP4 MoE quantizes activations with static scales; each
+    uncalibrated layer takes the max of the two nearest calibrated layers.
+    """
+    calibrated = [idx for idx in input_scales if idx not in uncalibrated]
+    for idx in uncalibrated:
+        neighbours = sorted(calibrated, key=lambda n: (abs(n - idx), n))[:2]
+        if not neighbours:
+            raise ValueError(
+                f"MoE layer {idx} has no calibrated NVFP4 layer to take its "
+                "input scales from."
+            )
+        scales = []
+        for i, input_scale in enumerate(input_scales[idx]):
+            scale = max(input_scales[n][i].max().item() for n in neighbours)
+            input_scale.fill_(scale)
+            scales.append(scale)
+        logger.info(
+            "MoE layer %d quantized from BF16 takes the input scales of layers "
+            "%s: w13 %.4e, w2 %.4e.",
+            idx,
+            neighbours,
+            *scales,
+        )
+
+
 class MuseMoERunner(MoERunner):
     """MoE runner that splices MuseSpark1x's post-expert norm into the experts."""

Could we use existing online quantization infrastructure here?

Namely:
- `--quantization-config.targets`:
```
     --quantization-config '{"targets":{"*layers.0.feed_forward.experts*":"nvfp4_per_token", "*layers.61.feed_forward.experts*":"nvfp4_per_token"}}'
```
- (re-)quantization of checkpoints https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/60276 https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/64378

In https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/32412 / https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/32029 and followup https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/52167, the goal is to have vLLM frontend not be dependent on the model producer library (modelopt, compressed-tensors, etc.), and if possible not on the model arch.

As muse spark MOE is a normal `RoutedExperts`, the API at https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/main/vllm/model_executor/layers/quantization/online is the one that fits naturally.

A welcome extension would be to have `Nvfpv4OnlineMoEMethod` & NVFP4 oracle compatible with Muse, if any change is needed (or have `MuseSparkNvfp4OnlineMoEMethod(Nvfpv4OnlineMoEMethod)`, alternatively, but using oracle would be cleaner)
